title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: About 98 MB that was never given back
summary: Three features keep the text of every project file in memory so they can answer quickly. Raising their ceiling over the last two releases took that from about 64 MB to about 98 MB on the project measured, and two of the three never gave any of it back.

highlights.title: The resource badge lets go
highlights.description: 40.8 MB across 6278 files, held for the whole session. Released on shutdown, on switching the badges off, and for a listing that lands after that.

highlights.title: The reverse string map too
highlights.description: About 17 MB with no release path at all. Built inline inside its registration, nothing could reach it.

highlights.title: No count without a listing
highlights.description: A zero computed across that moment would grey out a live resource. The badge reads ? usages and greys nothing instead.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The resource usage badge and the reverse string map now release the project listing they hold.
Both follow their setting at the moment the listing is written, not only when the work starts.
A guard in the test suite fails if either entry point goes back to building the hover provider inline.
